overall: Washington, DC has already reached 100.4°F as of 13:45 ET, essentially matching the NWS official forecast high of 101°F. The warming rate has stalled completely (+0.0°F/hr) with the intraday hour-of-max logged at 12:34 ET — roughly 1.2 hours ago — suggesting the temperature may be at or very near its daily peak. Severe thunderstorms are expected after 3pm, which would quickly end any remaining warming window and likely drive a sharp cooldown.
forecast_obs_notes: There is substantial model disagreement: NBM (100.6°F) and NWS (101°F) are tightly clustered near current observations, while GFS (107.7°F), ECMWF (105.4°F), and HRRR (104.0°F) skew 4–7°F warmer. The fact that the observed running max has already reached 100.4°F and stalled strongly validates the lower-end NBM/NWS guidance and argues against the higher NWP solutions, which would require a substantial re-acceleration that current surface observations do not support. The META model output (100% in the 84–85°F bucket) is a clear artifact — impossible given the observed temp — and should be disregarded entirely.
max_temp_prediction: The daily high is most likely to land in the 100–102°F range, with 101–102°F the central estimate. The temperature has stalled at 100.4°F and the trend slope (+0.959°F/hr) offers modest upside potential for a brief push before storms arrive, but the convective threat after 3pm sharply limits time for additional warming. The active even-bucket market's top bucket of 100–101°F at 27.0% is well-supported by current observations, though 102–103°F carries meaningful secondary probability (~25% per D1_NOW) if temperatures briefly accelerate before convection fires. Confidence is moderate-high that the final TMAX settles between 100°F and 103°F.
